blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines’ trade deficit with China reached $29.13 billion in 2025, exceeding its combined deficits with its next four largest deficit-generating trading partners and highlighting the country’s heavy reliance on Chinese goods amid continuing maritime tensions in the West Philippine Sea. According to data from the Philippine Statistics Authority cited in an analysis by Inquirer data scientist Dr. Alicor Panao, the Philippines imported $38.44 billion worth of goods from China last year while exporting only $9.31 billion. The country’s trade deficits with Indonesia, South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam totaled $25.29 billion, still less than its deficit with China […]...
